explanation: The new record's own cited article puts it first of four explanations of the collapse: "The first argument is that the Paris Peace Accords that ended the direct American participation in the war was seriously flawed, because it permitted the North Vietnamese to maintain their forces within territorial South Vietnam after the signing of the agreement, thereby dooming the ceasefire." A precondition and not a cause: the claim is that the agreement left the northern divisions where they stood and so made the offensive of 1974–75 possible, not that signing it brought the offensive about. `disputed`, because the article says in the same breath that this is one reading of four.

dispute.text: The article introduces it as one of four: "Four main lines of thought have remained particularly viable, all of which possess some validity, but all are also open to argument." Its other three put the collapse on "the refusal of the United States government to take promised military action in the face of North Vietnamese violations of the ceasefire", on a Congress that "simply wrote off and abandoned the Saigon government", and on "the American policy of Vietnamization as a prescription for defeat"; on those readings the terms of the agreement settled nothing either way.
